title: Slimline instrumentation: migrate to OTLP v1, trim logging hotspots, and reduce trace tail latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The runtime and control-plane services show intermittently high CPU and p99 tail latency attributed to observability code paths (blocking exporters, high-cardinality tag construction, and log formatting). Several services still run an older OpenTelemetry SDK and a custom trace shim that allocates heavily on request paths. This ticket aims to modernize the stack and remove performance anti-patterns without losing fidelity for debugging and SLO analysis.

Goal: Upgrade to OTLP/gRPC v1 SDK, replace the custom trace shim with the standardized propagation hooks, introduce a zero-copy log encoder for high-throughput services, and establish a migration plan that includes metrics parity checks, synthetic traces, and staged rollout. Target improvements: 20-30% CPU reduction in hot paths, 15-25% drop in trace-related allocations, and reduction of p99 trace export tail latency by 40% in worst-case scenarios.

Scope:
- Upgrade OpenTelemetry SDKs and exporters to OTLP v1 across runtime-core, request-proxy, and control-plane.
- Replace custom context shuttle in runtime-core with OTEL baggage/span context hooks.
- Introduce a pooled KV tagging helper to reduce transient allocations when constructing span attributes and log fields.
- Swap the production log formatter with compact, binary-friendly encoder behind a feature flag.
- Add an async, bounded trace exporter with backpressure signals to avoid blocking request threads.
- End-to-end tests and perf benchmarks, observability dashboards to track regressions.

Non-goals: Deep changes to retention/back-end (OTel Collector/Backends) or changing semantic conventions for major events in this ticket. Those will be separate follow-ups if needed.

2026-02-12 - Diego Morales: Did a quick prototype upgrade of runtime-core to OTLP v1 on branch feature/eng/otlp-upgrade. Observed ~12% CPU reduction on synthetic qps for span creation alone. Patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6421

2026-02-18 - Performance spike: CI load test showed trace exporter stalls when backend latency > 200ms. Decided to add an async bounded exporter queue and backpressure metrics (queue_length, drops). Added to implementation plan.

2026-02-20 - Design review (PM/Eng): PMs asked for a migration plan that preserves trace IDs and correlation for older spans when both old and new SDKs are in flight. Decided to keep trace-id format stable and add header compatibility shim in request-proxy.

2026-02-25 - Diego Morales: Implemented pooled KV helper (kvpool) and zero-copy tag concat. Microbenchmark shows 28% fewer allocations for hot request path. Benchmark gist: https://gist.github.com/diego/kvpool-bench
2026-03-01 - Security review note: SRE requested that the async exporter honor KMS-managed endpoints for OTLP export encryption. Filed dependency ENG-91234 for collector-side integration.
2026-03-03 - QA: End-to-end synthetic trace tests added to nightly pipeline. Observability dashboard panels created: dashboards/observability/otel-migration (internal link).

2026-03-05 - Diego Morales: First canary rollout completed for runtime-core in staging; CPU and p99 allocation graphs look good. Opened RFC to standardize semantic conventions for new tag names: https://docs.redwood.ai/rfcs/2026-03-otlp-tags
